title: A work-item read outside a transaction can report false corruption during a concurrent commit
outcome: A work-item read outside a transaction can report false corruption during a concurrent commit
acceptance: The full quality gates pass and a Codex and a Claude review are clean

load_work_item and latest_canonical_work_event_for_item_optional read the item row, its latest-event binding and the project feed head from one consistent snapshot, even when their caller is in autocommit (as SqliteStore::get_work_item is), without changing any refusal a genuinely inconsistent store still produces

work_service::update::tests::concurrent_gate_transitions_serialize_and_history_lookup_stays_bounded passes, and a deterministic regression test that commits a concurrent work event between load_work_item's reads (for example from a SQLite progress handler on the reading connection) fails before the fix and passes after it

completion.summary: Reads that compare several statements now run on one commit state, so a concurrent commit can no longer look like corruption. In autocommit, load_work_item and the latest canonical event lookup each run through on_one_snapshot; inside a caller's transaction nothing changes. work_read_snapshot shares the same helper. work_completed_by_restored_record and required_child_successor also read on one snapshot. Two deterministic trace_v2 reproductions pin the fix, and each fails without its snapshot: an evidence commit before the feed-head read ("latest-event binding differs from its indexed feed head"), and a revision committed between the row and event reads ("differs from its latest canonical event"). Landed as 391169d; three review rounds, the final one with no Critical, High, Medium or Low findings; installed as build a4c0b90d94ef. Broader audit of other composite readers filed as w-f0ca1bb7ef80.
